name: Coda
description: Read-only Coda access: token identity, docs, the tables in a doc and the rows in a table

tools.name: whoami
tools.description: Identify the Coda account and workspace this API token belongs to

tools.name: list_docs
tools.description: List the Coda docs this token can see

limit.description: Max docs to return (default 20, capped at 100 by this connector)

tools.name: list_tables
tools.description: List the tables in one Coda doc

doc_id.description: Coda doc ID, as returned by list_docs (e.g. AbCDeFGH)

tools.name: list_rows
tools.description: List the rows of one Coda table, with their cell values

doc_id.description: Coda doc ID, as returned by list_docs (e.g. AbCDeFGH)

table_id.description: Coda table ID or name, as returned by list_tables (e.g. grid-abcDEF123)

limit.description: Max rows to return (default 20, capped at 100 by this connector)

needs_review: base_url carries the /apis/v1 prefix ("https://coda.io/apis/v1") and tool paths are relative to it (/whoami rather than /apis/v1/whoami). Same requests on the wire either way, but it keeps the harness's control probe ON the API surface. With base_url "https://coda.io" the control path lands on Coda's marketing site, which answers 307 (verified by curl 2026-09-12); the differing status would let the harness read SHAPE_PROVEN off a website redirect, which proves nothing about the API routing.

The proof below is honestly AUTH_WALL, not SHAPE_PROVEN. Coda's auth wall sits IN FRONT OF routing: verified by curl 2026-09-12, /apis/v1/whoami, /apis/v1/docs, /apis/v1/docs/<bogus>/tables, /apis/v1/docs/<bogus>/tables/<bogus>/rows and a deliberately bogus /apis/v1/<control> path ALL answer a byte-identical 401 {"statusCode":401,"statusMessage":"Unauthorized","message":"Unauthorized"}. Host, TLS, the bearer scheme and the API's own error envelope are proven; the four PATHS rest on documentary provenance (tools_source) and can only be confirmed by a real token.
Auth kept exactly as scaffolded (bearer on api_token), which matches the vault registry entry's live-tested testHeaders (services/auth/config/integrationTypeRegistry.js key 'coda').

Category set to 'files_knowledge' to match the shipped taxonomy (google_docs, contentful, box, dropbox); the scaffolded 'uncategorized' is not a bucket any shipped spec uses, and the vault entry already labels Coda 'documents'.

The limit cap of 100 is OURS, not Coda's: the API documents `limit` as a maximum-results parameter without publishing a hard ceiling, so the clamp is a deliberate response-size guard. UNVERIFIED what Coda's own ceiling is.

Every response pick comes from the API documentation (tools_source), not from a live 2xx: no Coda account was held for this draft. list_tables and list_rows pick next_page_token so a caller can tell a truncated page from a complete one; if Coda omits it on a single-page response the field simply drops out. list_rows picks the raw `values` map, which is why truncate 2000 matters on that tool in particular: a wide table's cell payload is unbounded.
list_rows does not send useColumnNames, so `values` is keyed by column ID rather than by the human column name. Deliberate: column IDs are stable, names are not.
